"Netanyahu demands probe into sources for award-winning Gaza film NAZA"
BYLINE: "By Al Jazeera Staff and AFP" - AFP attribution. Photo credit: Ariel Schalit/AP.

Israeli PM BENJAMIN NETANYAHU called for an investigation into the anonymous sources featured in a documentary alleging Israel's military killed civilians in Gaza using AI-powered targeting systems.
The film, NAZA, draws on testimony from 24 UNNAMED ISRAELI MILITARY WHISTLEBLOWERS accusing the army of using the systems to kill numerous civilians.
Netanyahu on X, SATURDAY EVENING: "I demand that the chief of general staff, the head of the Shin Bet, and the attorney general launch a comprehensive investigation into the participants in the film 'Naza' and prosecute them for serious information security violations, criminal libel, and harm to Israel's diplomatic and security interests."
He added: "The film presents a false, misleading, and biased narrative that defames the State of Israel and the [Israeli military] internationally, severely damaging Israel's standing."
The Israeli military said in a statement last month it "categorically" rejected the whistleblowers' allegations, calling some assertions "absurd" and contradictory, and insisted the selection and approval of strikes "are made by human personnel only", in line with guidelines.
Israeli army Chief of Staff EYAL ZAMIR has called for legal action against the participants to be considered and ordered an investigation into suspected leaks of classified military information used in the film's production.
NAZA takes its name from the Israeli military term for civilian casualties expected in air strikes - an abbreviated form of the Hebrew phrase for "collateral damage".
Awarded a SPECIAL JURY PRIZE at the VENICE INTERNATIONAL FILM FESTIVAL; received a 25-MINUTE STANDING OVATION.
Directors YUVAL ABRAHAM and RACHEL SZOR have been accused of "treason"; the AP photo caption records the Hebrew word for "traitors" scrawled in graffiti over an image of the directors in Ashdod, Israel, on 15 September 2026.
